reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a clause at the preferred position — nothing is being over-flagged or edited.

The cited § 14.8 Personnel text addresses only each party's supervision/direction/control of its own personnel, IBM's assignment rights and subcontracting; it contains none of the rule's detection triggers ('shall not solicit', 'employ or engage', 'no-hire', 'induce ... to leave').

Because the preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer, treating the omission as compliant (rather than 'missing') is the correct classification — the gap favors our party and the rule expressly prefers no such covenant.

The failed deterministic sub-checks (12-month duration, general-solicitation carve-out) fail vacuously since there is no covenant whose duration or carve-outs could be measured; they are heuristics and do not undercut compliance here.

Rationale is accurate to the quoted text and the internal fallback guidance (mutual, personnel directly involved, 12 months, advertising/unsolicited carve-outs, no no-hire) is retained as evidence rather than raised as a negotiation issue, consistent with playbook handling of compliant findings.
